column1: # STEPS.tsv -- THE DESIGN-PLAN raku-roast-causes STEP TABLE (the cao, 2026-11-05; Lon in the coo's window: "I want CTO and CIO to share in the work and scrutinize EVERY SINGLE program and design the fix for the HQs." / "Each failing program is getting fixed today."; row raku-roast-every-red-program-triaged-and-its-fix-designed-by-the-cao). One step per CAUSE of Roast reds, measured by the cao's census (scrip m3 and rakudo unfudged per red program), each cure proven on a scratch worktree by a base-against-cure differential before it is written here.

# harness/scripts/test_design_raku_roast_causes_steps.sh reads it: --list prints it; --step N runs the step witnesses (this folder, .raku beside .ref cut from Rakudo 2026.05) in both modes, then the step probe tokens: moved=ERE@P1,P2 (none of the named roast programs has a latest mode-3 note matching ERE) | pass=P1,P2 (each named roast program PASS in both modes in its latest readings) | chapter=PREFIX:N | row=KEY:N | census=SYMBOL:N | smoke.
# executor hq_raku (Haiku): the ruling column is the whole change in words; the row GOAL repeats it as numbered steps with the exact text to type.

column7: X1: a double-quoted string whose whole body is ONE interpolated part ("$x", "$!", "@a[]", "%h<k>", "{ ... }") is a Str, as Rakudo stringifies it: today lower_interp_str in src/parsers/raku/rk_tree.c returns the interpolated node itself when no literal text surrounds it, so "$e" ~~ Str is False, "$!".WHAT is the exception class and "$!" ~~ /boom/ dies error 241 (pattern match left operand is not a string). CURE: at the end of lower_interp_str, after the last literal flush and before the return, when result is non-null and is neither TT_CAT nor TT_QLIT, replace it with expr_binary(TT_CAT, leaf_sval(TT_QLIT, ""), result). MEASURED by the cao on a scratch worktree (SCRIP 52f53c466 + the one line): witness red on the base, green on the cure in m3; base-against-cure over 339 roast programs (the 103 that contain a lone interpolation plus the 257 PASS programs): see the row LEDGER for the gains and that no PASS is lost.

X2: a colon pair whose value is in angle brackets (:lang, :x) is a NAMED argument of a call, as :x(...) already is: named_form in src/parsers/raku/rk_tree.c accepts TK_CP with ck v and cnt P only, so :x (cnt W) is built as a bare positional "y" (sub g(*@a, *%h) receives [1, "y"] and {}; f(:lang

, 1) binds "P" to $a). With :lang named, EVAL must take it: a call EVAL(src, :lang) is then built as __rk_named_call("EVAL", ...), which no EVAL arm in lower_raku.c sees, so the lowerer turns that named call back into the EVAL call with the lang value as a second argument, and bt___rk_eval throws for any language but Raku: X::CompUnit::UnsatisfiedDependency for Perl5 (Rakudo: Could not find Inline::Perl5), X::Eval::NoSuchLang "No compiler available for language 'L'" otherwise; both classes registered in rk_exc_init beside X::Cannot::Empty (without the registration the throw crashes in rk_exc_message: SIGSEGV, the cao measured it). The S01-perl-5-integration programs guard with try { EVAL("1", :lang) } and skip-rest: today EVAL succeeds and they run Perl 5 code. DEPENDS ON STEP 1: S29-context/eval test 14 reads "$!" ~~ /rt112472/, which dies error 241 until step 1 lands, losing tests 15-18. MEASURED on a scratch worktree (52f53c466 + this step): witness green m3; base-against-cure over the 126 roast programs that pass a colon pair with an angle value: ten S01 programs PASS (rc 0, every test ok), advent2013-day10 +3 ok, S06-signature/unspecified +2, S12-methods/chaining +1, S06-signature/types SIGSEGV becomes an honest short run, S29-context/eval -4 (step 1 cures it); every other program unchanged.

X4 (the cao, MEASURED on SCRIP 0c9eb2dad by --dump-ast): `$(my $x = 5; $x + 1)` dumps (TT_METHCALL (TT_ASSIGN x 5) "item") followed by an empty (TT_SEQ_EXPR): the paren term r_circumfix builds (rk_syntax.c, the contextualizer arms at 3666-3674; rkb_contextualize rk_tree.c 1667 only wraps what it is handed) keeps the first statement of a multi-statement semilist and drops the rest. Rakudo 2026.05: `( s1; s2; s3 )` is a List of each statement's value (`(@d»++; @d).elems` is 2) and `$( s1; s2; e )` is the value of the last statement (6). Cure in the build of the paren term: every statement of the semilist is kept, in order, as one node the lowerer reads (a fact of what the grammar matched, never a rewrite in rk_tree.c: skill raku section 7); `$( )` takes the last statement's value, `@( )` and `( )` the List. RakRungs stays 100.

X5 (the cao, MEASURED): rk_syntax.c 4310 registers every user infix at the fixed level PR('t') (additive) by add_user_op, and the traits r_traits reads afterwards (rtraits at 4418 lists equiv, looser, tighter) never change it: `10 mean 4 * 5` with `is tighter(&infix:<*>)` reads 15 (Rakudo 35), `is equiv(&infix:<*>)` 2 + 3 mul2 4 reads 20 (Rakudo 14). Cure: after r_traits, a sub named infix:<...> with `is equiv(&infix:<X>)` takes X's level and associativity; `is tighter` and `is looser` take a level just above or just below X's and no built-in level between (Rakudo's rule: the precedence string of X with a character appended, compared as strings); the user op's level is set before the program's later uses are parsed. The default (no trait) stays additive, as Rakudo's.

X6 (the cao, MEASURED): bt_samecase (src/runtime/by_name_dispatch.c 3967) walks UTF-8 BYTES and tests each pattern byte with ASCII isupper and islower, so a two-byte `ä` is neither and the pattern index drifts: 'Ab'.samecase('äÄ') reads Ab (Rakudo aB). Cure (skill raku section 7: the setting is Raku, a core method's C body deleted in the same landing): `multi method samecase(Str:D: Str:D $pattern --> Str:D)` written in Raku in the setting, per character of self taking the case of the pattern character at the same index or the last one (Rakudo src/core.c/Str.rakumod 2629 is the source); bt_samecase deleted, with its names in the by-name tables (by_name_dispatch.c 3426 and 14365) and in rk_is_str_subform (lower_raku.c 360). WAITS on raku-core step 7, the setting's first method on a core type (CTO-517).

X7 (the cao, MEASURED): .pairs on an Array builds rk_mk_pair(INTVAL(i), a.el[i]) over COPIES (src/runtime/by_name_dispatch.c 4238; the Hash arm 14315 likewise), so `for @a.pairs -> $p { $p.value += 100 }` leaves @a unchanged (Rakudo [117 123 142]) and %h.pairs the same. Cure (skill raku section 7: a run-time binding holds a REF to a heap Scalar, dereferenced in the box): the value of each pair .pairs yields over an Array or a Hash is the element's container, so an assignment through .value writes the element; written in the setting over the pull protocol, the C arms deleted in the same landing. .kv and .antipairs are not in this step.

X8 (the cao, MEASURED by --dump-ast): with `sub my($a)` declared, `my($x)` dumps (TT_FNC __rk_destructure ...), a declaration; Rakudo calls the sub (22). Raku's rule (Grammar.nqp, the term:identifier and the declarator tokens): an identifier directly followed by `(` with no whitespace is a function call, a declarator or keyword included when a routine of that name is in scope. Cure in the recognizer (rk_syntax.c, where the declarator `my` is matched): `my(` with a user sub `my` in scope is a call; `my (` with a space stays a declaration.

X9 (the cao, MEASURED by --dump-ast): `multi infix:<< - >>(e1, e2)` is declared (TT_SUB_DECL Rinfix_3c202d203e$2$e1$e2) and `e1 - e2` lowers to the builtin (TT_SUB e1 e2): -1 (Rakudo AWW). Cure: a program that adds a candidate to a builtin infix makes its use sites dispatch over the user candidates with the builtin as the fallback, through the dispatch box; never a by-name fallback or a strcmp on the operator (skill raku section 7). WAITS on raku-rewrite step 8 (bb_rk_dispatch, bb_rk_sig).

X10 (the vice_president, MEASURED on SCRIP 88686b571 while landing the coercion census; re-read by the cao on 12f2d7b18, red in both modes): `say 7 div True; say 7 mod True; say 3 mod True; say True div 2; say 9 % True` reads Failure Failure Failure 0 Failure, Rakudo 7 0 0 0 0. bta___rk_intdiv (src/runtime/by_name_dispatch.c) coerces a non-Int, non-Num operand through to_cstring then strtod, so True is the text True and reads 0.0. Cure: a DT_BOOL arm in bta___rk_intdiv taking 1 or 0 (INTVAL(x.i != 0)) for each operand, as to_real's arm does (R-656); no strcmp, no text road. The coercion census (util_coercion_surface_census.py) turns green with it.

X11 (the cao, MEASURED on SCRIP 12f2d7b18 in both modes; the cure proved green in both modes and the Raku smoke 10/10 on a scratch tree): `$ref<0>` on an Array, `@a{0}`, `(1, 2)<0>` and a Range held in a variable indexed `<a>` live and read (Any); Rakudo dies X::AdHoc with the message `Type Array does not support associative indexing.` (List and Range likewise, the type name the receiver's). TT_HASH_GET lowers to hash_get (src/lower/lower_raku.c, case TT_HASH_GET) and bt_hash_get (src/runtime/by_name_dispatch.c) reads only a DT_T table and returns Any for any other receiver. Cure: in bt_hash_get, directly after the rk_match_is line, a positional receiver (rk_sub_is_arr(args[0]) || rk_is_range(args[0])) throws rk_exc_adhoc of the message formatted with rt_mc_type_name(args[0]) and returns FAILDESCR. Not in the witness, separate causes: a Range LITERAL as the subscript's operand lowers as a generator (IR_TO), and a Pair's `<key>` reads (Any) where Rakudo reads the value. Entry S02-types/catch_type_cast_mismatch (not flipped by this step alone, CEO-2112).

X12 (the cao, MEASURED on SCRIP 12f2d7b18 in both modes; the cure proved green in both modes and the Raku smoke 10/10 on a scratch tree): `(^10).batch(0)` lives (the batch arm of src/runtime/by_name_dispatch.c maps a size under 1 to 1); Rakudo throws X::OutOfRange `Batching sublist length is out of range. Is: 0, should be in 1..^Inf` (Rakudo::Iterator.Batch). Cure: first line of the batch arm, an Int size under 1 throws (rk_exc_init then rk_exc_throw of DATCON_fn X::OutOfRange with message, what Batching sublist length, got the size, range 1..^Inf) and returns 1. It THROWS, it does not return a Failure: a sunk Failure is silent in SCRIP today (the CTO-514 silent-stop class). Entry S32-list/batch (not flipped by this step alone, CEO-2112).
